# Swirvo

> Swirvo is a free, fast, private file converter and PDF toolkit for Windows, written in Rust. Start dragging any file, tap Shift, and drop it on a format on a radial wheel; the converted copy appears next to the original. A full workspace (the Board) converts whole folders in parallel, and 59 tools cover PDF, Word, images, video and archives. Everything runs locally: no upload, no account, no telemetry. It also runs as an MCP server (`swirvo mcp`) so AI assistants can convert files and read documents locally.

Key facts:

- Platforms: Windows 10 (1809+) and 11 x64 (full app); Linux x64 (command-line tool `swirvo`).
- About 96 formats (138 file extensions): images (PNG, JPG, WebP, TIFF, HEIC, AVIF, PSD, RAW), documents (PDF, DOCX, ODT, RTF, EPUB, Markdown, HTML), spreadsheets and data (XLSX, CSV, JSON, YAML, XML), fonts, audio, video, subtitles, archives.
- PDF to Word rebuilds the layout; Word, Excel and PowerPoint to PDF work without Microsoft Office installed.
- PDF tools: merge, split (custom page ranges), compress, watermark, page numbers, Bates, protect/unlock (AES-256), crop, N-up, booklet, OCR (searchable PDF), redaction, forms, compare, digital signatures, PDF/A, PDF/UA.
- Originals are never modified; every conversion runs in a sandboxed worker process.
- License: the app is free to use (EULA); source code under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.
